plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your value minus a small increment. Since it's a single round, and we're assuming rational opponents, I will bid slightly below my value to increase the chance of winning without overpaying. Specifically, I will bid $46.50. This aims to win against bids lower than $46.50 while avoiding paying close to my true value.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your value multiplied by 2/3. This is because any bid above your value is irrational (you'd lose money if you win), and bidding significantly below your value risks losing the auction to someone bidding closer to their true valuation. Since this is round 1 and there's no history, I'll implement this 2/3 strategy. 33 * (2/3) = 22.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value minus a small amount. This is because any bid above your value risks winning at a loss, and any bid significantly below your value risks letting the item go for too little. Since it's round 1 and there's no history, I'll bid slightly below my value to encourage others to bid, while still aiming to win if their values are lower. I will bid $35.5.
